No, not directly. The JRC map (GFC2020 V4) is a snapshot of forest cover in 2020, so it can't show a 2023 loss. The 2023 loss comes from the Hansen/UMD dataset, which records 0.7 ha of tree-cover loss in 2023, about 1.2% of the 58.1 ha asset.

What JRC does show is that 100% of the loss area was mapped as forest in 2020. That means the cleared area was forest before the loss. This meets the run's corroboration rule, which requires at least 50% agreement. A later year of the series is also observed (data run to 2025).

The national forest map (MGAP 2021) classes 0.4 ha of the loss area as planted eucalyptus and 0.3 ha as outside mapped forest. None of it is native forest. This may be plantation harvest rather than deforestation.
